canal_p20_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_001.text: The forty-eighth morning brought the season's first argument about ice. There was no ice on the canal yet, only a pale skin in a puddle behind the grain house. A trader nevertheless wanted the winter toll estimate rewritten before he booked his next cargo. Han wanted the same estimate left alone until actual receipts changed. Luo wanted them both to stop standing in her doorway. Yue arrived with the closing work list and found the reserve applicant trying to make three conversations fit inside one account. Pei sent him to open the shutters instead.

canal_p20_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_002.text: The repaired gate reduced repeated check work. That saving helped keep future service affordable, but the old check worker had depended on those paid calls through autumn. He came with two finished upstream shift receipts and a question about winter. A trustee congratulated him on having more free time. His mouth hardened. "My room is not rented by the hour I dislike work." Yue looked at the trustee until the man stopped smiling. The worker asked to receive real task notices; he did not want a ceremony celebrating the disappearance of his income.

canal_p20_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_003.text: The two recent upstream shifts belonged to another employer's accepted work and had already been paid. They could not be presented as proof that every winter week was covered. Pei placed the man's requested contact on the current notice list, not on an invented salary line. Han said his private store needed a short inventory after the returned chest was opened. The work would be separate from the public gear lease and the existing repair allocations. He offered to show the actual hours and price later that day, allowing the man to decide whether so little work was worth taking.

canal_p20_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_004.text: A woman who washed crew clothes said winter always made this conversation arrive late. She had reduced laundry orders whenever boats stayed tied up, yet nobody described a cleaner canal as the cause of her empty wash tub. The check worker answered that his old tasks had been removed by a public decision. Their arguments were different and both touched the same cold months. Yue listened rather than merging them into a general hardship claim. The woman wanted the new job notice placed by the laundry steps too. That small request could actually be answered today.

canal_p20_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_005.text: Luo had promised no extra money for night checks and now had to tell a boat owner that plainly. He wanted one more late passage before the schedule restriction began after closure. His crew's private hours were his to price; the public receiving gap was not theirs to erase. He proposed paying for a limited additional receiver himself. The trustees asked for the actual competent person, safe route, and appointment before agreeing to consider it. He left to ask his own clerk. The answer might cost enough to make the daylight passage more attractive.

canal_p20_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_006.text: At the store table Pei reviewed Yue's ordinary accepted hours through the completed path work. Ten of her twelve equivalents had now been certified. Settling the wage book, including earlier paid portions used for food, brought her cumulative ordinary pay to twenty copper. Two equivalents and four copper remained for real closing work. Yue signed the cumulative total rather than receiving another twenty on top of the earlier payments. Her emergency wages belonged to their separate completed appointment. She had kept personal journey money apart; the public fuel box did not resemble a travel purse.

canal_p20_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_007.text: The clerk asked Yue whether she intended to remain for the winter charter's first month. Yue said her eight-week canal term ended on the fifty-sixth day. Her future orchard visit was still waiting for Ren's acceptance, and she would not solve one missed obligation by casually accepting another indefinite one. Luo heard this from the doorway and pretended to examine a hinge. Pei said the winter record invitation had received a promising applicant. The information made Yue glad and Luo oddly quieter. Both had grown accustomed to a particular spare chair being occupied.

canal_p20_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_008.text: Matron Ren's actual reply arrived at midday in Yue's named personal dispatch. She accepted the third morning after canal closure, the fifty-ninth day on Yue's current calendar, and the full review interval Yue had offered. Patients and the necessary staff had confirmed their availability. The retained earlier arrangement would govern the visit; Ren listed its relevant papers without inventing a duty every former route had promised. Any overdue personal return still required Yue to come in person. Yue read the acceptance twice, then carried it outside because the office suddenly felt too warm.

canal_p20_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_009.text: Tian found her beside the lock with the letter open. "Bad news?" she asked. Yue shook her head. "A door has actually opened." Tian leaned against the rail and waited. Ren had written no welcoming poetry, only a date, interval, and practical request to arrive rested enough to listen. Yue found this more moving than she expected. She had spent so long asking permission to repair a promise that she had almost begun to enjoy waiting. Now the ordinary journey and the actual people beyond it would have to replace her intentions.

canal_p20_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_010.text: The passage agent checked the two-day ordinary route for the fifty-seventh and fifty-eighth days. Three copper covered the named boat stages, with walking between the hill stops; no magical shortcut appeared in the price. Two lodging copper and two food copper made a seven-copper personal provision. Yue paid the three-copper booking from her cumulative earned ordinary wages and set aside the other four. The accepted fare did not spend the same coin twice. She retained an additional personal copper for an optional west-kiln stop only if her final route used the priced connecting cart.

canal_p20_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_011.text: The agent marked the reserved places and the ordinary cancellation terms on Yue's receipt. The west-kiln connecting stop, if chosen, fitted the same two travel days at the additional quoted copper; it would not move Ren's fifty-ninth morning. Yue checked the walking stages against her ordinary strength rather than imagining a burst of qi would rescue a late departure. She could carry her habitual pack, stop for the priced night, and reach the orchard pavilion without taking commission apparatus. The agent asked whether she wanted a faster advertised passage. She chose the route he had actually confirmed.

canal_p20_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_012.text: Luo read the calendar after Yue invited her to. She said the old orchard people would find Yue more irritating than last time because she now checked everything twice. Yue answered that this had always been true. The keeper put a finger beside the departure day, then removed it before smudging the ink. "I will not call you back because somebody hears a bell strangely." It was not a promise that nothing would go wrong. It was an offer to use the people and plans they had made. Yue thanked her without disguising her own relief.

canal_p20_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_013.text: The older orchard papers stayed in Yue's personal folder. She did not add the canal household register or the commission's test record to the journey pile. Ren held the actual clinic originals needed for review. The accepted appointment acknowledged the outstanding arrangement; correspondence had still not completed any owed physical visit. Yue wrote the departure and arrival dates on a small personal leaf. Tian said she should sew it to her sleeve so another request could not steal the space. Yue laughed, then put it beside the fare receipt where she would really look for it.

canal_p20_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_014.text: Han's wife visited the office to ask about the future gear lease receiving date. She had planned her private store hours around it and disliked being told she should be pleased merely because the deposit was returned. Pei showed her the accepted post-closure beginning, the monthly review, and the conditions under which the gear could be used. The woman checked every line. "His grand plans occupied the entire summer," she said of Han. "I would like the small one to occupy its actual day." Yue thought of Ren's letter and understood the request painfully well.

canal_p20_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_015.text: The new winter record applicant arrived before the scheduled office visit carrying spectacles wrapped in a worn cloth. She had copied grain deliveries for a merchant and wanted to know whether the short public job allowed her to keep that work. Pei showed the two weekly intervals and actual fee. The applicant checked them against her current employer's mornings. She did not apply for an imagined full clerkship. Her name was entered for the limited examination, pending the trustees' acceptance. Pei set out the broad-writing paper as if preparing a feast for somebody with unexpectedly sensible tastes.

canal_p20_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_016.text: The check worker took Han's private inventory offer away to consider. One equivalent of work, divided into two half-day intervals, would pay two copper from the merchant's current private receipts. It promised neither the winter season nor a public appointment. The worker asked whether the missing old night checks could return if boats were busy. Luo said new work would be priced if needed, not reinstated because a name once occupied the line. He seemed angry and relieved in alternating breaths. His younger sister wanted to borrow his coat; winter had already become practical at home.

canal_p20_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_017.text: Bao's ordinary follow-up was due that afternoon. His sister had asked Yue to walk with them only if her personal time allowed, and Bao had objected to needing an escort. The clinician had permitted light observation, not loaded carpentry; the visit would review the actual wrist rather than grant a deadline because the commission ended soon. Yue could accompany them after completing her named public interval. She remembered Bao laughing at crooked pegs while rain shook the roof. Neither gratitude nor affection had made the swelling disappear. That fact still seemed to annoy everyone except the clinician.

canal_p20_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_018.text: At the laundry steps the new task notice stayed readable only if it stood under the eave. The washing woman let the clerk use that dry place but asked him not to nail through her working rail. He tied the board to the public post nearby. Yue watched him leave an empty space for genuine future offers rather than names guessed into employment. Two boatwomen stopped to read it and asked who chose workers. He explained the actual invitations and current accepted jobs. One woman asked for a copied contact. The other said she had enough work already.

canal_p20_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_019.text: The winter gross estimate remained eighteen copper a month under ordinary traffic. Ice could reduce it, and a broken gear condition could change the cost. The eight operating copper, six reserve copper, and four eligible debt copper were a division of future receipts, not three invisible purses already filled. Han still wanted the fourteen payable installments counted as fourteen months. His wife pointed to the puddle outside. "You can ask winter to sign," she said. He did not laugh. After a moment he placed the actual-receipts clause back beside the sum.

canal_p20_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_020.text: A boy brought a notice from the canal's farther landing: a customer had promised three winter cargos if he could obtain a lower rate. Luo recognized the promise as a negotiation, not collected income. The trustees could consider the actual tariff without letting the proposed cargos pay today's costs. Yue almost admired how quickly everyone now distinguished the two. Then the boy asked for his messenger fee, and three adults reached toward the wrong cash box. Pei redirected them to the accepted office dispatch line with an expression so dry that Yue had to look out the window.

canal_p20_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_021.text: The winter applicant's employer agreed she could keep her grain-copying mornings and undertake the short public record intervals if accepted. She returned the reply before dusk. Pei prepared a examination using actual current folder tasks with copies, leaving private patient papers and disputed originals out of reach. The reserve receiver would show her the normal filing route. Yue was relieved to see two limited jobs joining without turning either person into a replacement for every departing helper. Luo, listening, asked whether the applicant could also remember where the keeper left her kettle. Pei refused to put that into the contract.

canal_p20_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_022.text: Tian carried the loft confirmation to her mother. The older woman wanted the quoted return travel written more plainly before Tian accepted the winter trial. Tian agreed to ask; passing the fitting would not force her to sign. Yue helped compose no part of the private bargain unless invited. The seamstress came back smiling at having argued without surrendering either her ambition or her mother's concern. She asked whether Yue's orchard return frightened her. "Yes," Yue said. "It will contain answers I cannot control." Tian said a sail fitting sounded unexpectedly merciful by comparison.

canal_p20_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_023.text: At Han's store the released chest had become a table for the short inventory offer. His private loading crew would not be ordered to contribute unpaid hours because the public dispute had embarrassed him. The check worker could accept the priced work or refuse it. Han placed two copper beside the written appointment to show the funds existed, then put them back in his own box until earned. Yue liked the visible offer more than another speech about employment. Han said he had begun to dislike speeches too, which made Tian laugh when she heard of it.

canal_p20_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_024.text: Pei asked Yue which last unfamiliar thing she wanted to understand before the closing week. It was an unexpected question. Yue had been choosing tasks according to danger for so long that curiosity felt indulgent. She named the winter work notices, Bao's actual recovery, and the practical orchard journey she had finally booked. Each occupied a different part of her remaining time. Pei said one could be her next interval and the others could continue through their own named people. "You are allowed to learn something because you will remember it," the clerk added, almost gruffly.

canal_p20_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_025.text: The three appointments fell across the forty-ninth day without pretending all were public work. The winter notice visit lay inside Yue's remaining commission hours. Bao's clinic walk was a personal offer he had accepted after complaining. The passage office could explain the booked route during its ordinary customer interval. Whichever she pursued first, the current acceptance of Ren's date and the paid fare already stood. A later choice would not conjure different obligations in the orchard. Yue wrote each task's real duration and refused the temptation to make the small calendar prettier by erasing rest.

canal_p20_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_026.text: Morning arrived with rain loud enough to fill the keeper's stove room. Luo had hung Tian's offered plant-care instructions beside her own recipes and accidentally watered a bowl of dried chilies while thinking about them. Tian rescued the bowl and declared the future plant appointment conditional on better labeling. Yue laughed until Luo handed her the wet cloth. The joke occupied exactly five minutes. Then the young keeper went to her accepted round, the office applicant went to Pei, and Bao's sister appeared with her brother's coat held like a defeated flag.

canal_p20_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_027.text: Bao complained that the coat made him look like a patient. His sister said this was an unusually accurate garment. Yue saw his good hand fasten it while the supported one stayed clear. The check worker passed them carrying Han's accepted inventory sheet; he had chosen the two half-day intervals and asked for payment only when completed. Behind him the passage agent's boy carried the current ordinary boat departure board. Three modest futures moved through the same muddy yard. None looked like the triumphant ending someone might have painted after the storm.

canal_p20_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_028.text: Yue checked Ren's letter once more before folding it away. The actual date was accepted, the three-copper fare paid, and four copper held for ordinary food and beds. There were still two travel days and a real visit ahead. The winter notice, clinic review, and journey preparation each offered a way to make the coming week more truthful. Luo asked whether she wanted tea before deciding. Yue accepted; she could spend the few minutes without charging them to an employer or hurrying toward the road. The rain made the cup's surface tremble.

canal_p20_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_029.text: When the rain eased, Yue stood beneath the keeper's eave with her coat buttoned. At the office, Pei was arranging the winter applicant's copied papers. Bao and his sister waited by the safe walking route to the clinic. At the landing, the passage agent was explaining a missed boat to an irate customer. Yue chose her first interval from these actual invitations. The other people had work and decisions of their own; her choice would bring a different conversation into the day, not freeze the rest of the town until she returned.

choices.text: Help Pei Fen settle the finite winter record appointment.
Accompany Bao Jun to his ordinary recovery review.
Check the booked orchard journey with the passage agent.

canal_p20_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_030.text: Pei greeted the winter applicant with the same grain weights the woman used at her private job. The familiarity relaxed her until the clerk placed a disputed delivery copy beside them. One figure had been corrected without a date. The applicant asked who had made the correction and whether a receiving note survived. Yue sat by the door. She had expected a quick display of competence; the woman instead spent three slow minutes refusing to guess. Pei's eyes brightened. It was a kind of accuracy she could imagine trusting on a cold evening.

canal_p20_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_031.text: The applicant read the two short weekly intervals again. The current closing-week work had an actual administrative allowance; winter continuation still needed separate funding. She would not leave her merchant employer on the strength of a phrase about future opportunities. Pei approved so vigorously that the woman looked surprised. "I have served under very generous promises," the clerk said. "They are difficult to eat." Yue asked whether a two-month limited appointment, if funded, would suit her. The woman said yes, provided the hours and duties stayed as narrow as written.

canal_p20_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_032.text: At the laundry steps the notice board had attracted three arguments and one genuine request for contact. Yue carried the current closing-week invitation there herself. The washing woman asked whether the old check worker had obtained a winter salary. Yue described Han's two half-day private inventory intervals and nothing more. "That will buy food, not winter," the woman said. She wanted his reduced work named plainly in the public summary. With his agreement the clerk could do that. The woman untied a wet sleeve from her rail and shook water onto Yue's boots by accident.

canal_p20_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_033.text: The check worker was counting store tarpaulins when they found him. He had accepted Han's price and was halfway through the first private interval. Yue waited until he set down the inventory pencil before asking about the public summary. He wanted the lost recurring checks described without publishing his household rent. Han agreed not to supervise the conversation. The man said he was pleased the gate worked and still angry about losing income. Yue wrote both statements, because neither canceled the other. He read them and changed one verb before permitting their use.

canal_p20_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_034.text: Han's wife checked the inventory at the end of the accepted half-day. A cloth bundle looked like three pieces until the worker unrolled it and found four. She verified the correction and recorded the completed interval toward the two-copper total. The worker asked to be paid for the whole job at once on completing the second interval, which Han accepted. Yue watched a private appointment become ordinary rather than charitable. The same man might still need winter work afterward. A real short job did not need to pretend it was a complete answer to deserve being done.

canal_p20_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_035.text: At the trustees' room two merchants proposed contributing two copper each toward the limited record post. Their current accounts could afford four; they did not offer an endless fund. Yue asked whether the money would come with a right to choose whose claims the clerk copied first. Both said no, and Pei made that condition explicit. The grant, once actually received, could cover two winter months at two copper per month for the short agreed intervals. The merchants looked relieved that the small sum had acquired a useful scale rather than become the beginning of a grand campaign.

canal_p20_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_036.text: The merchants returned with the actual four copper before the afternoon market closed. Pei counted them with the trustees' receiver and placed them in a separate marked administrative purse. They were outside the projected eighteen-copper monthly toll division and could not be spent again as gate reserve or loan service. The applicant examined the two-month terms, including the end date and no automatic unpaid continuation. She accepted after checking her existing grain-copying mornings. Yue witnessed the signatures. The chair she would leave behind now had a person and a finite task beside it.

canal_p20_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_037.text: Pei showed the new assistant where she kept the broad paper and where the office floor collected drafts. The woman moved the small lamp to a position that eased the clerk's reading. She asked before shifting the shelf, then improved its labels in handwriting larger than Pei's. The older clerk protested that she could still see perfectly well. Her assistant looked at the tiny dated receipt and waited. Pei sighed. "I can see that you will be disagreeable." "Only during the appointed intervals," the woman replied. Yue laughed hard enough to lose her place in the folder.

canal_p20_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_038.text: The learning girl arrived with a question about a sum she had copied at home. Her hour was not a job and would not be silently assigned to the funded assistant. Pei invited her to bring it next week at the accepted lesson time. The girl looked at the new woman's spectacles and asked whether numbers became smaller as clerks grew older. Pei ordered her to stop conducting inquiries without a notebook. The assistant smiled and showed the girl a broad date mark. Yue thought the office looked less like a room protecting one person's endurance from everyone's convenient expectations.

canal_p20_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_039.text: The winter work report named the finite four-copper grant, the two accepted months, the old check worker's actual private inventory, and his remaining need for paid notices. It did not call the coming season solved. Yue took the signed page to Luo, who read the assistant's hours first and the funding second. "Will she remind Pei to eat?" the keeper asked. Yue said that was a question for people, not another contractual task. Luo nodded and put a slice of pear beside the folder anyway. A useful relationship could still grow outside its wage line without the line disappearing.

canal_p20_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_040.text: Bao walked to the clinic more slowly than he wished. His sister had agreed not to hold his elbow unless he asked, which made him intensely aware of every uneven stone. Yue went beside them during her accepted personal interval. At the gate he stopped to inspect the new pavers and began explaining the bedding. His sister pointed toward the clinic. "You may diagnose the road after somebody diagnoses you." Bao complained that the road at least listened. Yue watched him turn away from a task he knew and toward a question he could not answer himself.

canal_p20_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_041.text: The clinician unwrapped the wrist support and asked Bao to show movements without forcing a grip. He could turn farther than at the last review, but pain returned when he tried to close his hand firmly. The clinician stopped that attempt and checked the tender side. The improvement did not permit loaded carpentry, gripping tools under strain, or a heroic final day. Bao stared at the wall while she spoke. His sister paid the review price from their private household money. Han's earlier one-copper first visit did not purchase every later bill or cancel Bao's right to seek care.

canal_p20_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_042.text: The clinician permitted short light movements, brief observation, and another review if weakness persisted. She did not give a guaranteed date for full work. Bao asked whether he might plane a narrow board. "With the hand you keep pretending does not hurt?" she replied. "No." Yue almost smiled and then saw his eyes. He wanted an ordinary act he could trust himself to perform. The clinician offered a gentle unloaded exercise to practice within the stated limit. It looked too small to count as work. Bao watched closely despite his disappointment and repeated it with his sound hand first.

canal_p20_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_043.text: Outside the clinic Bao said he was tired of everyone watching his wrist before his face. Yue answered that she had been watching his face when he asked about the board. He looked away. His sister went to buy the ordinary support cloth the clinician had recommended, leaving them beside the wall. Bao admitted he feared another carpenter would finish the last adjustment better. Yue said the mason had finished it competently, which made him wince more than sympathy would have. She stayed until he added, quietly, that this was preferable to finishing it badly himself.

canal_p20_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_044.text: They bought three small buns from their own money and ate beneath the clinic eave. Bao held his in the sound hand and let the supported wrist rest. A woman beside them was waiting for a child's fever review and had no interest in canal reputations. She asked him to move his chair away from the doorway. He did. Yue enjoyed how ordinary the request was. His injury could be inconvenient without becoming the largest fact in every room. He took the last bite and asked his sister whether the young carpenter had understood yesterday's bracket lesson.

canal_p20_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_045.text: The younger carpenter had understood enough to make one good waste-wood mark and two dreadful ones. Bao wanted to see them later, but agreed to a brief sitting lesson without gripping tools. His sister accepted that plan only after he said it back without enlarging it. Yue offered no qi treatment. Her stage-four practice remained a limited trained capability, not a way to mend strained tissue. Bao did not ask for a pulse to prove her concern. Instead he asked her to tell him when she left, rather than disappearing after the final report as visitors so often did.

canal_p20_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_046.text: Yue told him the booked two-day route and Ren's accepted fifty-ninth morning. He nodded at the ordinary travel stages. "No running to make the last boat?" "No." "No carrying a gate just in case?" She laughed and said the commissioned apparatus would remain with its keeper. Bao looked pleased to have found an instruction she could obey as easily as he could resent his own. He said he would come to the closing handover if the short seated interval still suited his recovery. Yue answered that the chair would be there without pretending to prescribe the wrist.

canal_p20_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_047.text: His sister stopped at the household store to price winter provisions. Bao sat on the public bench while she worked out what they could buy from their actual wages. The reduced loaded work meant he would decline a private job he had hoped to take. Yue did not offer canal money to replace an unearned private price. He asked her to carry his refusal to the carpenter who had invited him, stating the current restriction plainly. She accepted the small errand. It was a kindness that did not require either of them to act as if disappointment had disappeared.

canal_p20_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_048.text: The private carpenter answered with another offer: Bao could review a drawing for a short priced sitting interval next week if the clinician's limits still allowed it. No loaded work would be hidden inside that appointment. Bao chose to consider it rather than accept merely because he disliked refusing. Yue brought the written terms back. His sister read them and said they would fit only after his actual recovery review. The possible work remained possible. Bao kept the page under his sound hand and looked less ashamed of needing an answer that took time.

canal_p20_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_049.text: The clinic report returned to the commission only as the necessary work restriction, with Bao's approval. His private examination details and household provision choices were not copied into the public hearing. The loaded ban continued; brief light observation remained allowed. His accepted ordinary pay and emergency reallocation stayed as recorded. Yue watched him head home beside his sister, coat awkwardly buttoned but no longer treated as an insult. She went back to the lock with an unfamiliar gratitude for a day on which nobody had asked her to command anything that moved.

canal_p20_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_050.text: The passage agent spread the route board across a table smelling of tar and oranges. Yue's three-copper fare receipt covered the named ordinary stages on the fifty-seventh and fifty-eighth days. He showed her which departure depended on a tide and which was a fixed cart connection. The hill walking interval was longer than the map made it appear. Yue traced it with her finger and asked where travelers rested if rain slowed them. He named the actual covered stop. She wrote it down without assuming every little roof along the road would welcome an apprentice.

canal_p20_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_051.text: Another customer demanded the advertised faster passage, then discovered the fare did not include his heavy trunks. The argument occupied the agent while Yue checked her own habitual pack. She had no commissioned frame, charged stones, public records, or borrowed road gear to return midway. Her personal clothes, tablet, ordinary food, and retained orchard note fitted the load she knew she could carry. The small thread Tian had cut from waste cloth weighed almost nothing. She tucked it into her own sewing roll rather than turning it into a credential for the next place.

canal_p20_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_052.text: The agent's assistant priced the optional west-kiln connecting cart at one extra copper. It could make a short home stop within the same two travel days if Yue selected that final route. The departure after the stop was confirmed, not improvised around her feelings. She checked that reaching Ren's appointment still left an ordinary night's rest. The assistant had relatives near the kiln and began describing every possible lane. Yue asked for only the route she would actually use. He laughed and admitted his directions otherwise ended with the house where he preferred to eat.

canal_p20_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_053.text: The booked route had an ordinary contingency if the first tide boat was delayed: a later named boat still reached the paid night's stop within walking limits. A longer closure would require a real message to Ren and changed travel, not qi spent racing an unpriced road. Yue asked the agent to note the contact. His assistant thought this sounded pessimistic. The agent said good travel plans could tolerate one bad afternoon without treating it as a moral failure. Yue liked him for saying it and wished she had heard the sentence months earlier.

canal_p20_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_054.text: She visited the lodging receiver's stall to confirm the two quoted nights and their actual locations. The woman had kept one small sleeping place for the named traveler, payable from the two copper Yue had set aside. There was no meal included; the separate two food copper remained necessary. Yue asked whether arriving after dusk would close the door. The woman named the accepted interval and the ordinary bell at the entrance. Its signal meant a traveler had arrived. Yue laughed at how grateful she was for a bell allowed to mean only that.

canal_p20_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_055.text: A former valley worker recognized Yue beside the lodging stall. He asked whether she was going to the forest with the repaired bell frame. Yue explained that the commission's apparatus remained where it belonged and her next accepted visit was to the orchard. He seemed disappointed; rumors carried more interesting baggage than people. He told her he had heard the canal could now turn floodwater with lightning. She corrected the bounded work, rated pocket, and ordinary escape. He nodded slowly. "Still useful," he said at last. She was glad he did not need the story enlarged to keep that opinion.

canal_p20_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_056.text: At the market Yue bought a length of personal pack cord at its quoted price from her own money. The old cord was serviceable but had begun to fray near the knot. She cut only the worn end from it and kept the sound short piece for ordinary wrapping. The small private purchase did not require a new apparatus or promise. While checking the knot she remembered arriving at the canal eight travel days after the valley, confident that another investigation would help her delay thinking about the orchard. The road now led exactly toward the thought she had avoided.

canal_p20_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_057.text: The orchard acceptance asked her to arrive with the actual retained arrangement ready to discuss. Yue reread its separate duties before preparing her response. If her earlier personal return was owed, its lateness would be admitted in person; other arrangements retained their own questions. She did not compose an apology for promises she had never made. The difference felt less like a technical defense now that real patients would hear her answers. She wrote that she accepted Ren's full review interval and had booked the ordinary two-day journey. That letter confirmed preparation and no more.

canal_p20_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_058.text: When the personal message went out, the agent gave her a clean duplicate fare slip to keep apart from the first. She chose different places in her pack, remembering how one wet pocket could defeat two copies. The food and lodging provision remained four actual personal copper held for the road. The optional kiln fare remained another separate copper only if used. Yue counted the coins once, then stopped. She could spend the rest of the interval checking her coat and boots without asking numbers to reassure her about the conversation awaiting her at the orchard.

canal_p20_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_059.text: On returning to the lock Yue showed Luo the plain travel map. The keeper traced the ordinary walking stage and asked whether the hostel's kettle was clean. Yue admitted she had not examined it. Luo nodded with satisfaction at having found a flaw in the apprentice's preparation. Tian came in carrying a sample seam and said she would question the kettle next time. They laughed together over a plan whose essential parts were finally settled. Ren's accepted date stood ahead of them like a house with a real doorway, still requiring Yue to cross the distance and enter.

canal_p20_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_060.text: By dusk the reports had returned from the office, clinic, and passage stalls. The new assistant had accepted the limited record post after the actual four-copper merchant grant was received. Bao's clinician still barred loaded carpentry while allowing brief light observation. Yue's ordinary booked journey and Ren's accepted date remained unchanged. The three conversations differed according to where Yue had spent her interval, but the named people had completed their own parts of the day. Pei read the public notes while Yue kept the private clinic and travel papers out of the office folder.

canal_p20_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_061.text: The four supplemental administrative copper would pay two per winter month for the two short weekly record intervals. The grant had its own receiving count and end date. It did not enlarge the forecast eighteen monthly toll copper, take anything from the six-copper maintenance reserve, or disguise another debt payment. The assistant's private grain copying continued in its accepted mornings. Pei hung a broad new label on the shelf and then pretended not to admire it. Luo said she could read it from the doorway. The clerk accused them both of celebrating her decline with excessive enthusiasm.

canal_p20_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_062.text: Han's former check worker completed the second private inventory half-day before the store shut. The merchant and his wife checked the accepted list and paid the actual two copper from current private business receipts. The worker signed for one equivalent of private inventory work, separate from the commission's twenty-eight ordinary equivalents. His two recent upstream shifts stayed with their own paid account. Winter employment was still uncertain. He asked the new assistant to retain his contact for priced notices and went home carrying wages he had earned, which were more useful than another assurance of public gratitude.

canal_p20_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_063.text: The boat owner who wanted late winter passage returned with his clerk's price. It was enough to make the daylight booking preferable. He chose that actual slot rather than demanding an unappointed public receiver. Luo changed the cargo reservation and marked the unsupported late interval closed under warning conditions. The owner was annoyed, but his crew's private schedule now had a real route. Yue watched the decision and wondered how many old household duties had survived because an inconvenient price was easier to erase than to pay. Today somebody had finally allowed the inconvenience to remain visible.

canal_p20_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_064.text: At the keeper's stove room Bao sat for the short permitted evening visit he had chosen. His sister described the clinician's continuing limit only after he agreed. The wrist had improved but was not ready for gripping or loaded tasks. He would not perform an unpaid final feat to demonstrate usefulness at closure. Luo pushed the kettle toward Yue with a look suggesting that visitors should feed themselves. Bao said he could supervise the water from his chair. For once the joke did not tempt him into proving the remark with his injured hand.

canal_p20_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_065.text: Yue told them the orchard appointment aloud: the full review interval on the fifty-ninth morning, after two ordinary travel days following canal closure. Ren had actually accepted the patients' and staff's availability. The booked fare was three copper; four more remained held for food and the two nights. The optional west-kiln connection cost an additional personal copper only if chosen. These were her own earned funds and decisions. The commission would not owe her another journey because she happened to have delayed an earlier one. Luo listened more softly than she had read the calendar.

canal_p20_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_066.text: Any personal return still owed under Yue's earlier orchard arrangement remained unfinished until she went in person. Other retained arrangements kept their actual different duties. The accepted appointment repaired the scheduling failure and made a visit possible; it did not let a letter claim the visit's work. Yue repeated this to herself while putting Ren's note beside the ordinary fare slip. She did not know whether the matron would be angry. She knew where to stand when hearing the answer, and that knowledge made the fear feel more like part of a real road than a wall.

canal_p20_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_067.text: Tian's mother returned the winter trial offer with one passage marked. The loft had clarified the ordinary return travel and the resident forewoman's contact if Tian fell ill. Tian could now decide with those practical answers instead of borrowing Yue's courage. The actual fitting on the fifty-fifth afternoon still came first. Her mother said she would attend if the observer did not object. Tian laughed and said the sail was likely to perform better under such a threat. Luo asked whether the plant needed its own witness. The seamstress said only if the keeper intended to drown it again.

canal_p20_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_068.text: The limited assistant's appointment made Pei unusually talkative about past winters. She described a year when boats froze into the canal and the office still received demands for toll figures before dawn. Yue asked why nobody had helped her. "They did," Pei answered. "Then I made their help into proof I could always manage." She folded the new grant receipt carefully. A younger person would work beside her at named hours, not appear whenever she looked tired. She had agreed to say when the work exceeded those hours. The promise seemed to cost her more than the merchants' four copper.

canal_p20_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_069.text: Han's wife invited Tian to the private store to see the returned letters once the conservator released them. Han had not yet decided how much he wanted to share. The invitation stayed conditional on his actual agreement; nobody took silence as permission. Yue would be leaving soon and might miss the viewing. She accepted that possibility without asking the private drying work to hurry for her departure. A story did not become unfinished merely because she would not be present for every later conversation. She watched Han and his wife close the store together before turning back toward the lock.

canal_p20_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_070.text: The small apparatus remained disconnected. Its accepted earlier record carried the exact selected route balance and a conservative floor of two hundred forty-four charge units. No new draw had occurred during dry handover or path work. The eight stones stayed in commission custody. Yue's own cultivation was still Qi Gathering stage four, trained and limited as when she arrived. Luo no longer asked whether the borrowed fuel had made her stronger. The keeper was more interested in whether the box seal kept rain out and whether the appointed people knew when to leave the position alone.

canal_p20_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_071.text: The closing clerk copied the ordinary pay statement with Yue's cumulative twenty already settled and four remaining for two real work equivalents. The total would be twenty-four, not twenty added to another twenty-four at the end. Other accepted workers' earnings stayed within the fifty-six-copper line. Emergency labor remained its separate twenty-four-copper allocation, including the dated injury transfer. Yue checked her current hours because a fond farewell could otherwise turn several social visits into paid work. She had enough named closing tasks left to earn the balance without inventing more danger.

canal_p20_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_072.text: The lost winter checks remained in the public employment summary with the worker's chosen wording. The washerwoman's task-notice request also stood, without pretending her laundry income had been restored. The assistant would keep the board current only within the limited paid intervals and its ordinary safe delivery route. Future employers had to state their actual task, time, and price. Pei struck through an offer that said merely "willing hands wanted." The washing woman laughed when she saw the correction. "Now ask whether they want my hands attached to me," she said, handing the clerk a dry sleeve.

canal_p20_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_073.text: The garden household sent a brief reply approving the recorded warning receiver and rejecting a copied suggestion of future basin-watching duty. The reed household confirmed their closure contact for the season they remained nearby. The stall's nephew accepted the early purchasing contact. These names were people in arrangements they could explain, rather than inherited slots waiting for the next storm. Yue compared the replies with the rota and then stopped staring at it. There would always be a next correction. A usable document could carry one without demanding that she delay the orchard until every future person agreed.

canal_p20_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_074.text: Late that evening the public path officer brought the older route book requested for the failed boarding step. It included a reach beyond the grain sheds that newer copies barely showed. A narrow common access had served boats returning upstream, not the private store wall beside it. The winter warning plan now depended on knowing where that access remained usable. The officer proposed a bounded walk on the fiftieth day within his ordinary inspection appointment. Yue could use one of her remaining closing intervals to help compare the route on actual ground.

canal_p20_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_075.text: Luo looked at the forgotten reach and said she used to go there for a quiet supper when her household was noisy. Han said his father had stacked spare platforms along its dry edge. Neither memory settled today's public access or the condition of the bank. Yue liked the way the two recollections occupied the same little space without fitting together. The officer wanted current measurements, the surviving route reference, and an actual route people could walk. The low autumn light in the old book's marginal sketch looked nothing like the muddy yard outside.

canal_p20_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_076.text: Pei put the winter grant papers away before opening the route leaf. She refused to let the new discovery erase a completed administrative appointment from everyone's attention. The assistant checked the grant receipt, placed it on its broad-labeled shelf, and joined the reading only after her current accepted task ended. Yue followed the example and finished her own pay correction first. The officer waited without complaint. Work could change direction while preserving the tasks already done. At the table's edge Ren's personal letter remained folded under Yue's hand, a separate road she would not set down again.

canal_p20_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_077.text: The forty-ninth day ended without a great announcement. Bao went home to rest. Tian checked her real sail cloth and then watered the plant correctly. Han counted private winter orders. Luo inspected the ordinary lock during her accepted round, while the young keeper closed her stall. Yue tightened her personal pack cord and left it beside the appointed travel papers. From the farther reach came the creak of an old mooring line someone had forgotten to loosen. Tomorrow's walk would have to identify its owner before deciding whether the rope belonged where it stood.

canal_p20_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p20_078.text: Before sleeping, Yue wrote a short acknowledgment to Ren: the accepted fifty-ninth morning, the full review interval, and the booked ordinary route. She made no report of a visit already performed. Then she extinguished the lamp instead of composing three better versions of the same sentence. Outside, the repaired gate held its ordinary level; inside, her wrist felt only the ache of a day's writing and carrying. Her limited stage-four practice would travel with her because she had earned it. The charged stones, the public records, and the town's winter choices would remain here.
